Yard supervisors: 3,000 MXN per day covering fuel, tolls and minor parts, with minor parts capped below 2,000 MXN per transaction.
Mexican commercial team travel: 20,000 MXN monthly per person, physical cards, travel categories.
Administración office expenses: 5,000 MXN monthly per person, virtual cards. Software subscriptions are excluded and handled on the central software card — see the audit log.

All software and subscriptions company-wide on one virtual card held by Sistemas in Monterrey. 25,000 MXN monthly. The Brazilian branch must not contract software itself; requests route to Monterrey. Every new vendor requires Finance approval before the first purchase.
Fuel cards for the three Brazilian drivers starting October 2026. R$450 per day per card, accredited fuel stations. Cannot be activated until the Brazilian entity exists.
Brazilian commercial team travel: R$6,000 monthly per person. The team is not yet hired.
Brazilian office expenses: R$1,500 monthly per person.
Miami travel for commercial staff based in or visiting Miami: USD 1,200 per person per month.
Miami office expenses: USD 400 per person per month. Miami has no fleet in 2026, so no fuel programme exists; fleet spend requests are rejected and escalated to Monterrey.

approval_policies.name: Aprobaciones México
approval_policies.source: entrevista_descubrimiento_es.txt — Alejandra Vidal (CFO), [04:11]: "Hasta dos mil pesos, automático. De dos mil a veinte mil, aprueba el jefe directo. Arriba de veinte mil, apruebo yo." Local thresholds are 2,000 and 20,000 MXN; converted at 18.0 MXN to the dollar because this format expresses thresholds only in USD. See the audit log.

approval_policies.name: Nuevo proveedor de software
approval_policies.source: politica_gastos_2026.txt, section 2.5 — "Todo proveedor nuevo de software requiere autorización de la Dirección de Finanzas ANTES de la primera compra, sin importar el monto." Encoded at a zero threshold because approval rules trigger on amount; this therefore routes ALL software spend to the CFO, not only new vendors. See the audit log.

mcc_controls.translation_notes: 'Solo estaciones de combustible autorizadas. Sin excepciones.' mapped to Ramp category Fuel and gas (18). This is broader than the memo requires: it permits any station Ramp classifies as fuel, not only authorised ones. Ramp can restrict to named merchants once the list of authorised stations is supplied — raised in the audit log.
'Somente postos de combustível credenciados' mapped to Ramp category Fuel and gas (18), with the same broadening as the Mexican fuel programme: accredited stations are not enumerated in the packet.
'vuelos, hoteles, restaurantes, transporte' mapped to Airlines (4), Lodging (6), Restaurants (19) and Taxi and rideshare (8). Car rental (5) was not named and is excluded.
Centralised software mapped to the single Ramp category SaaS / Software (40). Cloud and infrastructure categories are not included because the packet does not mention them.
